subject: Re: Request: load profile & sampling plan for latency/throughput benchmarks
messages:
From: Aaron Moreno <ops@globex.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@globex.com, Priya Shah <benchmarks@globex-corp.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 08:13:00 -0700
Subject: Load profile & sampling plan request for RFP performance appendix

Hi Irene,

Thanks for agreeing to respond to the performance appendix. For the RFP scoring committee we need a brief, reproducible plan that describes:
- The traffic sampling windows you recommend (warm, steady-state, soak) and durations.
- Key metrics you will report (p50, p95, p99, token/s, reqs/s, CPU/GPU util, memory, batch occupancy).
- How you plan to exercise cold vs warmed KV cache and prefix caching impacts.
- A minimal set of synthetic and replay workload inputs (we can provide anonymized logs).
- Any noteworthy test harness constraints (e.g., client-side throttling, tokenization overhead).

Can you deliver a short runbook and a data sample CSV by EOD Thu (20 May)? The committee needs raw numbers to compare across vendors.

Aaron
Ops & Benchmarks, Globex
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Moreno <ops@globex.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Load profile & sampling plan request for RFP performance appendix

Aaron —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a first-pass runbook (redwood-load-profile-runbook-v1.pdf) and a sample payload CSV (test-sample-traffic.csv). High level summary below; the PDF contains step-by-step commands, benchmark harness flags, and expected data outputs so your team can reproduce results locally.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Windows: 10m cold/warm ramp, 30m steady-state (primary), optionally 2h soak for long-tail stability.
- Metrics: report p50/p90/p95/p99/p999 latencies (server-side token-latency and end-to-end), requests/s, tokens/s, GPU util, host CPU, GPU memory, batch size distributions, and KV-cache hit rate.
- Cache: Run three passes — cold start (cache empty), warm (single workload pass to warm prefix/KV cache ~5–10k requests), and hot (sustained steady-state). Provide per-pass deltas.
- Workloads: 1) Short prompt (avg 30 tokens), 2) Long prompt (avg 300 tokens), 3) Reranker batch (50 inputs), 4) Multi-turn chat synthetic (20% context reuse).
- Harness notes: we recommend client workers with tokenization done client-side to isolate tokenization overhead; include a small separate measurement of tokenization CPU cost. Use continuous batching (we provide harness flag --enable-continuous-batching) and vary batch target sizes 1/4/8/16 to capture throughput curve.

Open items where we need your input:
1) Do you prefer raw per-request logs (CSV) or aggregated histograms (HdrHistogram)? We can supply both but CSV is larger.
2) Will you provide an anonymized request log for replay, or should we generate synthetic inputs?

I'll loop in Marcus for kernel/hardware notes and Laura for the commercial framing. We can meet Tue AM if you want a walkthrough.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2026 09:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Load profile & sampling plan request for RFP performance appendix

Team — forwarding Globex's ask plus my initial draft. Short turn here (they want reproducible numbers by Thu EOD). Marcus, can you validate the runbook's kernel selection notes (quantized model behavior, batching targets) and confirm any caveats around multi-GPU packing and seq-limited sharding? Vivek, please add any SLO/observability flags we should require in their harness to capture tail-latency root causes. Laura, aware they'll use numbers in the scoring matrix — flag any phrasing we should avoid in the public deliverable.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2026 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Load profile & sampling plan request for RFP performance appendix

Irene — quick tech notes after reviewing the PDF: 
- Quantization: our 4-bit kernels exhibit ~8–12% token-latency variance for long-context runs relative to fp16 on very long sequences (>=1024). Call this out with the model/quantization matrix.
- Sharding/packing: for dedicated runs where they request multi-GPU packing, include a note that p99 can increase if CPU-to-GPU PCIe congestion occurs at bursty ingress; recommend pinning to one socket and using NVLink when possible.
- KV-cache warm: measure KV cache warm by tracking unique key insert rate; recommend a warm pass size of 10k distinct session prefixes to get stable hit rates.
- Batching ecology: provide per-worker target batch and an observed occupancy histogram; we should deliver a script in the harness to serialize this.

I'll add these as an appendix and attach a short script snippet for occupancy histograms. Please let me know if you want me to join the walkthrough with Globex.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Load profile & sampling plan request for RFP performance appendix

Team —
Good notes. Two commercial cautions:
1) Please avoid publishing absolute cost-per-token numbers in the RFP appendix; provide normalized unit metrics (e.g., tokens/sec per GPU-type) and reference the test configuration. Globex will use these in the scoring model and we want apples-to-apples.
2) When we provide p99s, include the exact stimulus (prompt length distribution, concurrency, batch targets) as a short table so reviewers can interpret tail latency differences.

Irene, I'll prepare a one-paragraph cover note that frames the results (what they can and cannot infer from the run). Marcus — if you can include a short caveat line for the quantization matrix that suffices for reviewers.

Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Engineering
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Moreno <ops@globex.com>, Priya Shah <benchmarks@globex-corp.com>

Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Load profile & sampling plan request for RFP performance appendix

Aaron / Priya —

Thanks for the quick turnaround window. Attached are the runbook and sample payload CSV we discussed. Summary of deliverables and next steps: 

Deliverables (attached):
- redwood-load-profile-runbook-v1.pdf — step-by-step test harness commands, recommended warm/steady/soak windows, batch target matrix, and OBSERVABILITY flags to capture occupancy and kernel-level metrics.
- test-sample-traffic.csv — 200 synthetic rows reflecting short/long/multi-turn/reranker cases; ready for replay.

Key assumptions called out in the runbook:
- Tokenization is measured separately; client-side tokenization recommended to avoid server-side jitter.
- Per-pass warmup recommended: cold (no cache), warm (10,000 unique prefixes), hot (30m steady-state).
- Report buckets: p50, p90, p95, p99, p999 latencies both as token-latency (server processing) and end-to-end.
- Include occupancy histograms and per-worker batch size distributions in outputs (we attached a small script in the PDF appendix).

Open asks for you:
1) Confirm whether you want raw per-request CSVs or HdrHistogram exports.
2) If you can share an anonymized 48-hour inbound log we can generate a high-fidelity replay; otherwise our synthetic CSV is designed to approximate typical SaaS chat workloads.

We can host a 30m walkthrough Fri 21 May 08:00-09:00 PT or Mon 24 May 09:00-09:30 PT — let me know which works.

Best,
Irene
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
